doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Starting a piece from a verbal cue
summary: A trick learned from Dave: take a speech rhythm or phone number and bring it into music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. But you have — you might have a title in mind, you’re commissioned, so I’m just trying to envision that first time you sit down at the piano how does it direct the first thing you try to do. Or maybe it doesn’t.

Both. I guess the first thing very often will be a trick I learned from Dave which is to see if there’s a verbal cue, maybe a speech rhythm. It’s just like we used to learn phone numbers. Like my phone number now, I got a SIM card a few days ago so as not to forget it, it’s 9534437 so I think okay well that’s sort of like mid-period Stravinsky, right?
So you know I’ll grab something from outside of music and try to bring it into music and then see if that does something.
